verified: Google DeepMind launched Humanity's First Exam, a reliability benchmark that Google's blog says uses 544 prompts; The Decoder reports that it tested 18 models and that even leading systems such as OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra stumbled when asked for 16 consecutive correct answers, with visual perception accounting for 73% of errors.
unconfirmed: The full per-model scores, the exact 73% error breakdown across all 18 models, and the finding that more compute time does not fix the failures have not been independently replicated; those details rest on The Decoder's account and Google's benchmark description, and the report does not provide the underlying paper or a complete results table.

verified: Google DeepMind 发布了名为“Humanity's First Exam”的评测，共包含 544 道日常题，并公开了部分数据集（Google 官方博客）；The Decoder 报道称，该评测考察了 18 个模型，关键在于要求模型对同一类任务连续 16 次答对，而不只是答对一次。
unconfirmed: 哪些模型具体在哪些任务上失败、报道中提到的 GPT-6.2 Astra 等模型的相对位置，“视觉感知占 73% 的错误”和“增加算力时间并不能解决问题”这两项结论，目前都只见于 The Decoder 这一篇二次报道，现有报道未链接 DeepMind 的原始论文、排行榜或完整结果表；另有一条 YouTube 短视频称配套的 Kaggle 竞赛为期三周、截至 12 月 15 日、奖金 5 万美元，也缺少第二个来源佐证。

titles.en: DeepMind's "Humanity's First Exam" finds top models fail repeated everyday tasks
titles.zh: DeepMind“人类首次考试”：顶尖模型难连续答对16题
